answer: Each node commits to its challenge setup before a future drand quicknet pulse; the threshold-BLS signature then seeds the task and its verification rules, so no participant can choose a favorable pulse or precompute answers. Fresh, unpredictable tasks make offline farming by automated sybil swarms costly, while commit-reveal exposes changed submissions. A lagoon, grove, or vault may label a task domain, but identity resistance still depends on admission controls and resource costs.
